situacion.es: Quieres pedirle ayuda a un compañero.
situacion.en: You want to ask a colleague for help.

opciones: Could you help me, please?
Help me now.
You must help me.

explicacion.es: «Could you..., please?» es la forma educada de pedir algo.
explicacion.en: 'Could you..., please?' is the polite way to ask for something.

situacion.es: Llegas tarde a una reunión.
situacion.en: You arrive late to a meeting.

opciones: Sorry I'm late.
I'm late. Start again.
Why did you start without me?

explicacion.es: Basta con disculparse: «Sorry I'm late».
explicacion.en: A simple apology is enough: 'Sorry I'm late'.

situacion.es: Un compañero te ha ayudado con un bug.
situacion.en: A colleague has helped you with a bug.

opciones: Thanks a lot for your help!
OK.
Finally.

explicacion.es: Dar las gracias siempre suma; «Finally» suena a reproche.
explicacion.en: Saying thank you always helps; 'Finally' sounds like a complaint.

situacion.es: No entiendes lo que ha dicho alguien en una llamada.
situacion.en: You don't understand what someone said on a call.

opciones: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
What?
Speak better.

explicacion.es: «What?» a secas suena brusco; mejor pedir que lo repitan.
explicacion.en: A bare 'What?' sounds rude; ask them to repeat it instead.

situacion.es: Quieres que alguien revise tu código.
situacion.en: You want someone to review your code.

opciones: When you have a moment, could you review my pull request?
Review my pull request.
Review this now, it's urgent for me.

explicacion.es: «When you have a moment» respeta el tiempo del otro.
explicacion.en: 'When you have a moment' respects the other person's time.

situacion.es: No puedes ir a la reunión de mañana.
situacion.en: You can't go to tomorrow's meeting.

opciones: Sorry, I can't make it tomorrow. Could you send me the notes?
I'm not coming.
Your meetings are boring, so no.

explicacion.es: «I can't make it» es la forma natural y educada de decir que no puedes ir.
explicacion.en: 'I can't make it' is the natural, polite way to say you can't come.

situacion.es: Encuentras un error en la web de un compañero.
situacion.en: You find a mistake on a colleague's web page.

opciones: I think there's a small typo on the home page.
Your page is full of mistakes.
Who wrote this rubbish?

explicacion.es: «I think...» y «small» suavizan el comentario.
explicacion.en: 'I think...' and 'small' soften the comment.

situacion.es: Necesitas más tiempo para terminar una tarea.
situacion.en: You need more time to finish a task.

opciones: I'm sorry, but I need one more day to finish this.
It's not finished. Deal with it.
Stop asking me about it.

explicacion.es: Te disculpas y das un plazo concreto.
explicacion.en: You apologise and give a clear timeframe.

situacion.es: El código de un compañero tiene un problema de rendimiento.
situacion.en: A colleague's code has a performance problem.

opciones: This works, but it might be slow with big lists. What do you think about using a map here?
This is slow. Rewrite it.
Did you even test this?

explicacion.es: En una code review: reconoce lo bueno, explica el problema y propón con una pregunta.
explicacion.en: In a code review: acknowledge what works, explain the issue and suggest with a question.

situacion.es: Tu jefa te pide algo que hoy no puedes hacer.
situacion.en: Your manager asks for something you can't do today.

opciones: I'd love to help, but I'm working on the release today. Could it wait until tomorrow?
No, I'm busy.
That's not my job.

explicacion.es: Dices que no, explicas por qué y ofreces una alternativa.
explicacion.en: You say no, explain why and offer an alternative.

situacion.es: Un cliente se queja de que la web va lenta.
situacion.en: A client complains that the website is slow.

opciones: Thanks for letting us know. We're looking into it and will update you soon.
It's fast for us, so the problem is you.
The website is fine.

explicacion.es: Agradeces el aviso y dices qué vais a hacer.
explicacion.en: You thank them and say what you will do.

situacion.es: Quieres interrumpir a alguien en una reunión.
situacion.en: You want to interrupt someone in a meeting.

opciones: Sorry to interrupt, but could I add something?
Stop talking, I want to speak.
Wait, wait, you're wrong.

explicacion.es: «Sorry to interrupt» es la fórmula para pedir la palabra.
explicacion.en: 'Sorry to interrupt' is the set phrase for asking to speak.

situacion.es: No estás de acuerdo con la propuesta técnica de un compañero.
situacion.en: You disagree with a colleague's technical proposal.

opciones: I see your point, but I'm a bit worried about how this would scale. Could we look at alternatives?
That's a terrible idea.
No. We're doing it my way.

explicacion.es: «I see your point, but...» reconoce su idea antes de discrepar.
explicacion.en: 'I see your point, but...' acknowledges their idea before disagreeing.

situacion.es: Un compañero lleva una semana sin responder a tu email.
situacion.en: A colleague hasn't replied to your email for a week.

opciones: Just following up on my email from last week. Any thoughts?
Why are you ignoring me?
I've told you a hundred times.

explicacion.es: «Just following up» recuerda algo sin presionar.
explicacion.en: 'Just following up' is a gentle reminder.

situacion.es: Tienes que decirle a un cliente que una función se retrasa.
situacion.en: You have to tell a client that a feature is delayed.

opciones: Unfortunately, the new feature will be delayed by a week. We apologise for any inconvenience.
The feature is late. Sorry not sorry.
Your feature is late because of your changes.

explicacion.es: «Unfortunately» y la disculpa formal son lo esperado con clientes.
explicacion.en: 'Unfortunately' and a formal apology are what clients expect.

situacion.es: Alguien ha cometido un error en producción.
situacion.en: Someone has made a mistake in production.

opciones: Let's focus on fixing it first, and then we can look at how to prevent it.
Great job breaking production.
Who's responsible for this?

explicacion.es: Primero arreglarlo y luego prevenirlo, sin buscar culpables.
explicacion.en: Fix it first, then prevent it, without looking for someone to blame.

situacion.es: Rechazas una petición de un cliente importante.
situacion.en: You're turning down a request from an important client.

opciones: I'm afraid that falls outside the scope of this project, but we'd be happy to discuss it as a separate piece of work.
We won't do that.
That's a ridiculous request.

explicacion.es: «I'm afraid...» suaviza el no, y ofreces una salida.
explicacion.en: 'I'm afraid...' softens the no, and you offer a way forward.

situacion.es: Das feedback a una persona junior que ha cometido varios errores.
situacion.en: You're giving feedback to a junior developer who has made several mistakes.

opciones: You've made real progress. There are a couple of things to work on, so let's go through them together.
You made a lot of mistakes again.
Maybe this job isn't for you.

explicacion.es: Empiezas por lo positivo y planteas la mejora como algo compartido.
explicacion.en: You start with the positive and frame improvement as a shared task.

situacion.es: Tu manager propone un plazo poco realista.
situacion.en: Your manager suggests an unrealistic deadline.

opciones: I'd like to flag a risk: with the current scope, that date looks tight. Could we discuss priorities?
That's impossible, forget it.
Fine, but don't blame me when it fails.

explicacion.es: «Flag a risk» y «looks tight» señalan el problema sin enfrentarte.
explicacion.en: 'Flag a risk' and 'looks tight' raise the issue without confrontation.

situacion.es: Quieres pedir un aumento de sueldo.
situacion.en: You want to ask for a pay rise.

opciones: I'd like to discuss my compensation, given the responsibilities I've taken on this year.
Pay me more or I'll leave.
Everyone earns more than me. It's unfair.

explicacion.es: Lo planteas como una conversación y lo justificas con hechos.
explicacion.en: You frame it as a conversation and back it up with facts.
